title: Google Search Engine: Complete Architecture
description: Design a scalable Google-style search engine with monolith and microservice architectures using React, ASP.NET Core, Azure, and AWS.

data.text: Design a scalable Google-style web search engine. The system must continuously crawl the web to discover new pages, parse and index content for fast retrieval, process user queries with relevance ranking, generate descriptive snippets, and support autocomplete and spell correction. It must handle billions of pages, serve thousands of queries per second, and return results in under 300ms while maintaining index freshness.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Web crawler discovers and fetches pages from the internet while respecting robots.txt and crawl budgets
Indexer extracts text, metadata, and links from crawled pages and builds an inverted index
Search API accepts queries with operators (AND, OR, phrase search, site:) and returns ranked results
Ranking algorithm scores results using PageRank, TF-IDF, BM25, and machine-learned features
Snippet generator extracts relevant text around query terms for result descriptions
Autocomplete service suggests queries as users type based on popular searches and personal history
Spell checker detects misspelled queries and returns corrections with 'Did you mean?' suggestions
Safe search filters adult or explicit content from results
Image, video, and news verticals provide specialized search experiences
Search analytics track query volume, click-through rates, and result quality

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Query response time must be under 300ms at p99 for standard web search
System must crawl and index the entire publicly accessible web (100B+ pages)
Index must be updated incrementally within minutes of page changes
Search service must handle 40,000+ queries per second globally
99.99% availability for the search API
Index storage must be efficient; compressed inverted indexes should fit on commodity hardware
Crawler must be polite: respect rate limits, crawl delays, and avoid overwhelming servers

data.text: Start with a monolithic ASP.NET Core application that handles crawling, indexing, and search in a single process. Store crawled documents and an inverted index in a relational database. This validates the core search pipeline before moving to distributed storage and processing.

data.text: As the web grows, split the monolith into microservices specialized for each phase of the search pipeline. Crawling, indexing, and query serving have very different scalability profiles and should be scaled independently.

items: Crawler Service: Discovers and fetches web pages using BFS/DFS with politeness delays. Respects robots.txt, maintains per-domain rate limits, and stores raw HTML in blob storage. Publishes CrawlCompleted events for indexing.

Indexer Service: Parses HTML, extracts text and metadata, removes stop words, and builds an inverted index. Runs as a distributed MapReduce or Spark job. Stores posting lists in a compressed, sharded format for fast intersection.

Search Service: Accepts queries, parses query operators, retrieves matching document IDs from the inverted index, and returns a candidate set to the Ranking Service. Handles paging, filters, and safe search.
Ranking Service: Scores candidate documents using BM25, PageRank, and ML-based features (click data, freshness, user location). Returns the top-K results sorted by relevance score.
Snippet Service: Extracts and formats relevant text segments from matched documents. Highlights query terms and ensures snippets are concise and contextually accurate.
Query Analyzer: Processes raw queries for autocomplete, spell correction, query expansion, and intent classification. Suggests corrections and popular related queries.

- Debounced query input to reduce API calls during typing
- Cached autocomplete results for recently typed queries
- Virtualized result list for smooth scrolling through thousands of results
- React Query for caching search results with stale-while-revalidate
- Intersection Observer for infinite scroll pagination
- Web Workers for client-side query parsing and highlighting

data.title: Search Service (ASP.NET Core)

cards.title: Compute
cards.description: Run crawler workers, indexer jobs, and search API servers
pros: Scale crawler fleet horizontally across thousands of URLs
Spot instances reduce cost for batch indexing jobs

cards.title: API Gateway
cards.description: Rate limit and route search API requests globally
pros: Edge caching for popular queries reduces latency
WAF protection against scraping and abuse
cons: Cache hit ratios depend on query diversity

cards.title: Cache
cards.description: Cache frequent queries, autocomplete results, and document metadata
pros: Reduces load on the ranking and snippet services
cons: High cardinality queries may not benefit from caching

cards.title: Database
cards.description: Store crawled documents, metadata, and query logs
pros: Massively scalable for billions of document records
Low-cost archival for raw crawled content
cons: Complex queries require secondary indexes or separate search engines

cards.title: Storage
cards.description: Store raw crawled HTML, images, and index snapshots
pros: Cheap, durable storage for petabytes of crawled data
Lifecycle policies for archival and deletion
cons: Index rebuilds require reading from cold storage

cards.title: Messaging
cards.description: Queue crawl jobs and index update events
pros: Buffers crawl requests to avoid overwhelming target sites
Decouples crawler from indexer for async processing
cons: Queue depth can grow during crawler backlogs

data.title: When to Choose Microservices?
data.text: Start with a monolith. Split into microservices only when you have clear scaling bottlenecks, independent deployment needs, or team boundaries that justify the operational overhead.

data.title: Summary
points: Search engines are pipeline-heavy: crawling, indexing, and query serving must be decoupled for independent scaling
The inverted index is the core data structure; its compression and sharding determine query performance
Ranking is the most computationally expensive stage and benefits from ML model optimization
Crawl politeness is a first-class concern; aggressive crawlers get blocked by target sites
Start with a monolith to validate the index schema, then extract Crawler, Indexer, and Search as separate services
data.takeaway: Google Search Engine is a distributed system. Start simple, then scale horizontally with microservices, caching, and managed cloud services.
